generated_from: visual review of 40 candidate contact sheets

status_definitions.primary_candidate: Best visual fit; must still receive slot annotation and native fill verification.
status_definitions.secondary_candidate: Useful for the target but not default.
status_definitions.reference_only: May provide artwork or page ideas; not a default automation family.
status_definitions.hold: Do not route new decks here until a stronger visual review or redesign.

academic-clean.notes: 02-005 is the modern restrained default. 01-003 remains for soft thesis defense only, not technical research.

ai-industry.notes: Use 02-005 as the native visual family. Add selected chart pages from 04-004 only after restyling/localization; 04-008 is for internal AI KPI reviews, not external research.

investor-pitch.notes: 02-005 is closest to modern investor/strategy tone. 01-007 is an older business-plan structure and requires redesign, evidence-first rewriting, and removal of 2017-era visual signals.

data-boardroom.notes: 04-008 has KPI, issue and action patterns. Its blue glossy visuals are serviceable for internal Chinese reports but must not be the external premium default.

brand-company-profile.notes: 02-001 is the professional editorial default for company profiles, design/architecture/agency proposals. Use 03-008 only for hospitality, luxury or leadership-story openings.

marketing-event.notes: Route culture, tourism, education and event storytelling to Chinese-style families; retain their special-purpose identity rather than forcing corporate charts into them.

wedding-bridal.notes: 03-007 is the most restrained vintage-album family; keep it strictly for wedding, venue, anniversary and bridal contexts.

career-portfolio.notes: Dedicated resume/portfolio use only; exclude from reporting, technical and investor routes.

generic-corporate.notes: Older corporate families remain usable for low-stakes internal reporting; they are deliberately not global defaults.

risks: fine gray detail needs contrast check

hard_rule: No family is animation_ready until reusable text/image shapes are explicitly named slot_* and a copied/fill deck plays successfully in Microsoft PowerPoint.
